clue.text: The best tool to choose

definitions.meaning: the ... of the bunch is the finest of a group
a pointed digging implement, as used on hard ground

explanation.surface: Advice on which implement to opt for.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run side by side, each a sense of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a noun for the choicest item, a noun for a digging implement and a verb for selecting.

clue.text: A couple of excellent reviews for Thomas, say

indicators.note: the review word is written twice in succession

parts.note: a puff is a piece of extravagant praise for a show or book

explanation.surface: Two glowing write-ups for a certain Thomas.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas the Tank Engine is a children's storybook locomotive, and puff-puff is nursery talk for a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish word for a steam train, of which the storybook engine Thomas is an example.

clue.text: Ran, in a way, ie provided food around noon

indicators.note: the word for supplying meals surrounds the letter for midday

parts.note: to cater is to supply meals

explanation.surface: A caterer hurried, serving lunch around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that canters moves at a gait between trot and gallop, a particular way of running.

clue.text: Doctor accepted as trainee astronaut

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician has been taken on for astronaut training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, the person accepted; it is a verb telling you to rearrange ACCEPTED AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase originally meant a youngster training for space travel, before its jokey sense of a dreamy person.

clue.text: Burns bridges, for example (but extra capital is needed)

definitions.text: Burns bridges, for example (but extra capital is needed)

parts.words: Burns bridges, for example (but extra capital is needed)
parts.note: read 'Bridges' with a capital B and Burns and Bridges become two surnames of versifiers, Robert Burns and Robert Bridges

explanation.surface: Cutting off ties is an example, the clue admits, if we capitalise another word.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'burns bridges' misleads; Robert Burns was the Scottish national bard and Robert Bridges a Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns and Robert Bridges are both famous writers of verse, examples of the plural answer.

clue.text: Holding one's own dated cutting tool

parts.note: to be coping is to manage well under pressure
to have seen someone romantically is to have dated them

explanation.surface: A tool that is old-fashioned but still manages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dated' looks like old-fashioned, describing the tool; it means went out with, SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine-bladed bow saw for cutting curves in wood.

clue.text: Feudal lord reckoning ally has a point

parts.note: a count is a reckoning of numbers
a pal is a friend or ally
a tine is a prong or point, as on a fork

explanation.surface: A medieval noble, calculating that a friend holds an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a medieval nobleman holding royal powers within his territory, a lord under feudalism.

clue.text: Old-fashioned types perform acts

parts.note: to do a task is to perform it
does is a verb form meaning acts or carries out

explanation.surface: Old-timers put on a show of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct birds give the figurative sense of people hopelessly behind the times.

clue.text: Angry words from one caught in traffic

indicators.note: the numeral letter is trapped inside the commerce word

parts.note: traffic as a noun can mean trade, especially illicit dealing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Furious shouting from someone stuck in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests a road jam, but it means commerce, TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a torrent of furious words.

clue.text: Trick that punishes, in a way, opponents at bridge

parts.note: a court that punishes may impose monetary penalties
in bridge the players are named by compass point, and South and East sit on opposing sides
in bridge the players are named by compass point, and South and East sit on opposing sides

explanation.surface: A card-player's ploy that penalises the other side at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South partner each other against East-West, so South and East are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge this word names a tactical play to win a trick, and more broadly any clever ruse.

clue.text: Offending motorist also a drug dealer?

definitions.meaning: a driver who habitually goes too fast
speed is slang for amphetamine, so a merchant in it would sell drugs, hence the query

explanation.surface: A driver who breaks the law and also peddles narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a habitually fast driver, and literally read is a seller of amphetamines.

clue.text: Goods taken from place below

parts.note: PL is a standard abbreviation for place, as in street names
beneath or lower than

explanation.surface: Merchandise removed from a site lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot or booty is goods seized, often by force, which is what the noun means.

clue.text: Persevere over each period before play starts

indicators.note: the phrase for persevering is laid over and around the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: to press on is to keep going despite difficulty
EA is the usual abbreviation for each, as on price labels

explanation.surface: Keep going through each stage before the action begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means wrapped around, not on top: the persevering phrase is opened up to hold the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport the weeks of warm-up and friendlies before the competitive campaign begins carry this name.

clue.text: Show a particular inclination? That's about right

indicators.note: the word for having a leaning goes round the letter for right

parts.note: 'that' points back to the definition, whose other synonym, to tend, is the outer piece

explanation.surface: A question about leanings, answered with a remark that it's roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' stands for the opening phrase: TEND also means show an inclination, and it goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this word means to incline in a certain direction, as prices or opinions do over time.

clue.text: Deploy bellicose-sounding military leader

parts.note: to field troops or players is to put them into action

indicators.note: the word for warlike is heard rather than written, giving a title that shares its pronunciation

parts.note: warlike, as in martial arts or martial law

explanation.surface: An instruction to send in a commander who sounds aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the highest rank in the British Army, a senior commander of armies.

clue.text: A couple of lines added to a committee's announcement before leaving platform

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two are LL
a board is a committee of directors

explanation.surface: A board adds two lines to its notice before quitting the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'platform' suggests a stage or speaker's dais; it is a railway platform as the train leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the call made by a guard or conductor telling passengers to board before departure.

clue.text: At riot I'm involved as faithful follower

indicators.note: involved in the sense of entangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A loyal follower joins in a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier follows faithfully what someone else does, closely reproducing it.

clue.text: Island criminal group covering racket up

indicators.note: the gang word wraps around the noise word

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese organised-crime gang

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: racket as a noise, a din

explanation.surface: A gang on an island is covering up a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means reading bottom to top, so the noise word is turned before the gang wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Bird, ie chicken, hit hard

parts.note: chicken in the sense of cowardly, for which yellow is slang
to strike with great force, as with a heavy tool

explanation.surface: A fowl, namely a hen, has been struck forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like a bird beside 'Bird', but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a European bunting with a bright golden head, a familiar farmland songbird.

clue.text: Priests holding mass for old festival

indicators.note: the word for the clergy keeps the mass letter inside

parts.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist monks or priests
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Clergy celebrating mass at a traditional feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas, on 1 August, was the old English harvest festival of loaf-mass.

clue.text: Religion some cherish in Tokyo

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A faith some people hold dear in Japan's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous faith of Japan, centred on worship of kami spirits.

clue.text: A medic going round hospital for a particular purpose

indicators.note: the word for a doctor encircles the hospital letter

parts.note: doc is a casual word for a doctor
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor making ward rounds with a definite aim.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase describes something arranged for one specific need, not planned in general.

clue.text: China's second-rate, at first, in this sport

indicators.note: places the word for inferior at the front, before the china name

parts.note: poor quality, inferior
Minton is a famous English make of porcelain

explanation.surface: The quality of crockery is poor, at least initially, in this game.
explanation.walkthrough: MINTON is a Staffordshire pottery and porcelain firm, so it can stand for china.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Democrat is top officer in party

parts.note: D stands for Democrat in US politics
CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: A politician is the senior official at a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political after 'Democrat'; it is a dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a social dance event, one sense of a party.

clue.text: Universal symbol found in Asian city, mostly

indicators.note: only most of the city name is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: Mandalay is a city in Myanmar (Burma)

explanation.surface: An emblem of everything discovered in a Burmese city, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist art this circular design represents the cosmos, hence a symbol of the universe.

clue.text: The seed, scattered, fell densely

indicators.note: seeds scattered are strewn about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Sown seed was strewn about and came down thickly.
explanation.definitionFit: When rain comes down in broad heavy masses it is said to fall like this.

clue.text: Noticed popular pet that's sweet

parts.note: spotted means seen or observed
a dog is among the commonest household animals

explanation.surface: Someone saw a well-liked animal that's adorable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like an adjective for the pet; it means a pudding. Spotted dog is a British suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a sweet is a dessert, and this is a currant-studded steamed suet pudding.

clue.text: Provide stimulation in one of the basic subjects in school

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the group word, as a pupil is inside a school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so R stands for one

explanation.surface: Encouraging pupils in one of the core lessons at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests a classroom but means a group of whales, a pod.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or urge someone into action, a form of stimulation.
